title: NAV to Business Central: What Actually Moves, and What Needs to Change?
summary: Moving from Dynamics NAV to Business Central requires two separate projects: a technical upgrade through mandatory waypoints (version 14 and 25) followed by cloud migration via data replication. The process demands converting C/AL customizations to AL extensions and evaluating whether to do a full migration or reimplementation, with data only moving as far as code does.
key_points: NAV to Business Central migration is two sequential projects: upgrade first through version 14 and 25 waypoints, then replicate data to online via Integration Runtime
Code does not replicate automatically; customizations must be converted to AL extensions installed on both on-premises and online for data to migrate
Every NAV version requires different numbers of upgrade hops (NAV 2018 needs two, NAV 2009 needs four), determining timeline before migration begins
Choose between full migration (all data and customizations) or reimplementation (essential data only) based on regulatory needs, historical data importance, and customization value
Third-party integrations, solutions, and custom tables need conversion to cloud equivalents or replacement before assessment is complete

quotes.text: It isn't one move. It's an upgrade, then a migration
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the fundamental misconception that NAV migration is a single operation, establishing that version upgrades must precede cloud data replication

quotes.text: Your data travels only as far as your code does.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the central dependency between code conversion and data migration, essential for scoping realistic project scope and outcomes
